drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna not open with the burnt offering?
outcomeNote: the answer falls outside this unit

segments.he: פַּר וְשָׂעִיר שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים כּוּ׳. מִכְּדֵי צָפוֹן בְּעוֹלָה כְּתִיב, נִיתְנֵי עוֹלָה בְּרֵישָׁא!
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: With regard to «the bull and the goat of Yom Kippur,» their slaughter is in the north and the collection of their blood in a service vessel is in the north. The Gemara asks: Why does the mishna list these sin offerings first? «After all,» while the halakha that slaughter must be in the «north» of the Temple courtyard «is written» in the Torah «with regard to a burnt offering» (Leviticus 1:11), the Torah does not explicitly state that the other offerings must be slaughtered in the north. Therefore, «let» the tanna of the mishna «teach» the halakha of «a burnt offering first.»
